hook.text: A lot of it was recorded late at night, once the voices had warmed up or the band had loosened up at its cocktail hour.

facts.label: Recorded
facts.value: July 2006, at Ed Droste's mother's house on Cape Cod

facts.label: Players
facts.value: Christopher Bear (drums, vocals, xylophone, lap steel, glockenspiel), Edward Droste (vocals, keyboard, autoharp, guitar), Daniel Rossen (vocals, guitars, banjo, piano, autoharp), Chris Taylor (clarinet, flute, saxophone, vocals, keyboard, bass, electronics and treatments)

sentences.text: Grizzly Bear was a solo name for vocalist Ed Droste, and Horn of Plenty, released in 2004, was a solo effort.
After that, the name grew into a full group, with Horn of Plenty collaborator Christopher Bear, Chris Taylor and Daniel Rossen joining Droste.
Christopher Bear said that putting a band together for live shows changed the dynamics and instruments, and helped them find a band sound.
Unlike Horn of Plenty, every member of the four-piece had a hand in writing and producing this record.
After about a month of basic tracking, each member added overdubs on their own, and some of them took a long time.
Christopher Bear said some of those parts would have been hard with everyone in the room, or with the meter running at a studio.
Daniel Rossen's arrival gave the band two main songwriters, and Christopher Bear said the mix of four members' ideas changed the sound most.
Droste and Chris Taylor said the lyrics have no real theme, but the album is about the band learning to work together while recording in that house.
Between 2007 and 2011, Adult Swim used several of the album's songs as bumper music, and 'On a Neck, On a Spit' appeared on Reaper, a show on The CW.
The first single, 'Knife', came out in May 2007 with an alternate edit of 'Easier' on the other side.
Warp20 (Recreated), a 2009 compilation, included Pivot's take on 'Colorado' and Jamie Lidell's take on 'Little Brother'.
In 2012, Daniel Rossen recalled that the four of them had been young and eager about making their first record together.

listen_for.text: Owen Pallett wrote and played the strings on a tune by Droste's great aunt that the band tried to slow down.
G. Lucas Crane contributed tapes to this track.
